facts.text: Three Rivers takes its name from the meeting of the Joseph, Rocky, and Portage rivers at its center.
Neal Ball, the first MLB player to pull off an unassisted triple play, once played for Three Rivers’s semi‑pro team in 1901.
Gregory’s Abbey, a Benedictine monastery of the Episcopal Church, was founded in Three Rivers in 1946 and remains a historic landmark.
Public education in Three Rivers is served by the Three Rivers Community Schools, a district that has been operating since the early 20th century.
Private schooling options include Immaculate Conception School and Heartwood Renaissance Academy, both offering alternative curricula within the city limits.
The city’s river system feeds into Lake Michigan, making the surrounding wetlands a popular spot for birdwatching and nature walks.
